description: Rear lower ground floor extension with first floor access stair. Provision of bin store to front garden with under croft storage. Installation of AC condenser unit to rear garden.
decision_conditions:
<p>All new external-facing and roofing materials in respect of all the works hereby approved (and any other incidental works carried out in this connection) shall match those of the existing building in respect of materials used, detailed execution, and finished appearance, including type, size, colour, bond, pointing, coursing, jointing, profile and texture.</p><p>

REASON: To preserve or enhance the character and appearance of the conservation area.</p>

Prior to superstructure works, detailed specification, a drainage layout and a management & maintenance plan (where applicable) of the permeable paving shall be submitted to, and approved by the LPA, in consultation with the LLFA. If soakaways i.e. plastic modules and soakaway rings are used, an infiltration test must be carried out to ensure that the capacity of the soil is suitable for infiltration. It must be demonstrated that there will be no increase in surface water flow being discharged offsite and an overall reduction in peak flow rate and volume.REASON: To mitigate against the impacts of surface water flooding.

A scheme for the provision and implementation of flood resilient and resistant construction details and measures for the site against surface water flood risk shall be submitted to and agreed, in writing with the LPA in consultation with the LLFA prior to the construction of the measures. The scheme shall be carried out in its entirety before the extension is occupied and; constructed and completed in accordance with the approved plans in line with current best practices.REASON: To mitigate against the impacts of surface water flooding.

The use hereby permitted, or the operation of any building services plant, shall not commence until a post-installation noise assessment has been carried out to confirm compliance with the noise criteria (Condition 10). The scheme shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details and attenuation measures, and they shall be permanently retained and maintained in working order for the duration of the use and their operation. Reason: To protect the amenities of adjoining occupiers and the surrounding area.

Detailed drawings/full particulars of the proposed development showing the matters set out below must be submitted to and approved by the local planning authority, in writing, before any work is commenced. The development shall not be carried out otherwise than in accordance with the details thus approved, which shall be implemented in full prior to the first use of the development and retained in perpetuity: a) details and materials of the privacy screening to be added to the side elevation of the proposed balcony facing No.9  Speldhurst Road to  a minimum height of 1.7m.  REASON: To protect the privacy and amenity of the adjoining dwelling at No.9 and reduce any opportunities for overlooking.

<div style="color: rgb(34, 34, 34); font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: small;"><b>Hedgehog Highway&nbsp;</b></div><div style="color: rgb(34, 34, 34); font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: small;">Within 1 month of the completion of the development hereby approved, the applicant shall provide adequate evidence of installed hedgehog access holes along the boundary fencing. The evidence shall include: A minimum of 1 Hedgehog Hole where a wall or fence is to be used as the boundary treatment, with such hole meeting the standards, unless that boundary is directly adjacent to a public road with no meaningful verge or footpath. Each hole must be at ground level and must create a gap through the fence or wall of approx. 13cm wide and 13cm high. Larger holes to be avoided. Each hole must have an appropriate sign near the hole to educate on the purpose of the hole, e.g. a small sign with the words "Hedgehog highway - please keep open". The hole should not be located near drains or other wet areas, or in any area which would require a hedgehog to 'step up' to reach it.&nbsp;</div><div style="color: rgb(34, 34, 34); font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: small;"><br></div><div style="color: rgb(34, 34, 34); font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: small;">Reason: To support and preserve endangered urban biodiversity, by providing habitats.</div>

<p>Part A: Prior to commencement of works, full details and specifications of the green roofs shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. Green roofs shall be planted with flowering species that provide amenity and biodiversity value at different times of the year. The submission shall include the following:</p><p>Detailed drawings of a roof plan identifying where the green roofs will be located and the measurement of their coverage; this should include other structures on the roof including roof lights and access points where applicable, and their relationship with the green roof; </p><p>The design of the green roof should be in line with GRO’s code of best practice; Section drawings demonstrating a minimum substrate depth of no less than 80mm for a sedum roof; </p><p>Details of the proposed type of invertebrate habitat with a minimum of one feature per 30m2 (where applicable for sedum roofs); which could include areas of bare, unplanted substrates, log piles, boulder or stone piles, sand piles or containers; </p><p>Details of the drainage system for the roof;</p><p>Details of the planting mix, including a minimum of 9+ species for sedum roof; All roofs to be sown with a wide mix of species; the roof should not rely on one species of plant life; and&nbsp;</p><p>Management and maintenance plan, including access arrangements, irrigation, and general maintenance actions.</p><p>Part B: Within a month of the first occupation of the development, evidence must be submitted to and approved by the local planning authority that the green roof has been delivered in line with the approved details unless otherwise agreed in writing. </p><p>The green roof shall be retained thereafter for the lifetime of the development in accordance with the approved management and maintenance plan.</p><p>REASON: To promote biodiversity on site through green roofs.</p>

Any plant shall be installed, together with any associated ancillary equipment, so as to prevent the transmission of noise and vibration into neighbouring premises. The rated noise level from all plant and ancillary equipment shall not increase the existing background noise level (10dB below) when measured 1m external from the nearest residential or noise sensitive premises. An assessment of the expected noise levels shall be carried out by a suitably qualified (IOA accredited) and experienced acoustic consultant, in accordance with BS 4142:2014+A1:2019 ‘Methods for rating and assessing industrial and commercial sound,’ and any mitigation measures necessary to achieve the above required noise levels shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority in writing for approval. The plant shall thereafter be installed and maintained in accordance with the approved details. Reason: To protect acceptable local noise levels
